items.summary:
During an interview on NBC's Meet the Press, Louisiana Republican Senator John Kennedy invoked Greek mythology to describe former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reported affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang (Huang Le), calling it "the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy." The remark came in response to host Kristen Welker's question about whether national security was at risk given Nvidia's central role in the AI boom. Huang stepped down as CEO on 12 November following allegations involving extramarital relationships with Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.

The reported affair connects to broader export-control concerns: Megaspeed International, where Alice Huang served as executive director, facilitated approximately $12 billion in chip sales that allegedly violated US restrictions prohibiting advanced AI chips from China. National intelligence director Jay Clayton stated on CNN's State of the Union that he suspected China obtained Nvidia's most advanced AI chips and told Fox News Sunday that "there are chips that have ended up in places that they should not." Kennedy said his focus was less on Huang's personal conduct than on how China circumvented export controls, directing questions toward Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

The article notes that Lutnick faced scrutiny for allegedly ignoring warnings about Megaspeed smuggling chips to China, while other administration officials reportedly wanted to blacklist the company but commerce department stalled enforcement. Kennedy characterized commerce leaders as either incompetent or knowingly complicit and called for them to testify under oath before a Senate committee. Bessent told CBS News's Face the Nation that the Trump administration had contacted Nvidia's temporary management and lawyers to determine who oversaw compliance, stating it "behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this." The piece also observes that Kennedy is known for his colloquialisms and southern drawl despite holding degrees from Vanderbilt University, the University of Virginia School of Law, and Oxford University.
items.title: Louisiana Senator John Kennedy Characterizes Jensen Huang's Alleged Affair as 'Most Expensive Sex Since Helen of Troy'

items.summary: NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to run inside vehicles on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor rather than in datacenter GPUs. The model is marketed as approximately 2B parameters—comprising a 2.45B backbone paired with a 0.2B diffusion action expert—though Hugging Face metadata lists it at 3B; its context length was not disclosed but measured prompt reached about 3,236 tokens. It converts surround-camera video into plans spanning up to 6.4 seconds and is the in-car counterpart of the larger Alpamayo 2 Super cloud model (about 34B). The architecture draws on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge with a Nemotron-based backbone and includes a SigLIP2 encoder, reading inputs from six cameras across 22 frames plus navigation instructions and 20 historical ego poses to output 64 waypoints. Training combined offline distillation from Alpamayo 2 Super-generated Chain-of-Causation autolabels using roughly 115,000 hours of multi-camera driving video and about 3.7 million traces, followed by closed-loop reinforcement learning in AlpaGym. Performance highlights include approximately 15.15 km per at-fault incident in the AlpaSim simulation (about 60 times Qwen-Drive-1.0's 4B model), with open-loop minADE of about 0.52 to 0.53 meters; however, it trails Alpamayo 2 Super and Qwen-Drive on LingoQA at a score of 75.2 versus the cloud model's 79.2. Latency figures range from 160 ms to 190 ms for pixel-to-trajectory planning under an FP8 TensorRT recipe, though PyTorch BF16 inference runs much slower at about 0.76 Hz in NVIDIA's demo video and the optimized pipeline reaches roughly 13 Hz in simulation; real-time performance on Thor requires this FP8 optimization rather than raw PyTorch execution. Validation is limited to a single H100 (measuring about 12.06 GiB peak memory) for workstation reference, with other GPU architectures unvalidated and context length undisclosed. The release also included AlpaJudge, an RL reward that reportedly improved reasoning quality by roughly 10% to 11%, distributed under the OpenMDW-1.1 license with Apache 2.0 code.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A Compact Reasoning VLA for Autonomous Driving

items.summary: In response to Sim Eng Cheong's October 19 letter proposing that ActiveSG replenish members' credits to $100 annually, Sport Singapore chief Tan Hock Leong declined the specific suggestion while outlining existing measures designed to keep Singaporeans active. Rather than adopting automatic annual top-ups, SportSG describes a broader approach centered on affordable facility access, varied programmes for different needs, and incentives for healthy behaviours. ActiveSG gym entry fees are set at $2.50 for adults (with lower concession rates for students and seniors), while swimming pool entry is $1 for adults; members aged above 65 receive free access to all gyms and pools. New members receive an initial $100 in credits, and existing members may carry forward unused credits provided they make at least one transaction each year. Additionally, since September 2026, Health Promotion Board Healthpoints can be converted into ActiveSG credits, offering another pathway to earn credits through healthy behaviours. Tan Hock Leong noted that SportSG will continue reviewing its facilities, programmes, and support measures to help Singaporeans integrate sport and physical activity into everyday life.
items.title: ActiveSG Chief Responds to Proposal for Annual $100 Credit Top-Ups

items.summary: In a forum response following Brazil's 7-0 victory over Singapore, writer A. Thiyaga Raju argues that rare fixtures against elite opposition should be deliberately used to develop young players rather than being judged solely by the scoreline. While acknowledging the value of experienced players like Hariss Harun and goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud, he contends that even 20 to 30 minutes against Brazil's world-class squad could provide valuable lessons in speed, movement, positioning, decision-making, and composure under pressure—experiences difficult to replicate domestically. He frames such friendlies as platforms for nurturing emerging talent 'carefully, deliberately and with the future in mind,' while noting he is not advocating fielding an entirely inexperienced team or disregarding experience. The piece presents these views as opinion rather than established fact; no concrete data on player development outcomes was provided.
items.title: Singapore Football Forum: Using Marquee Friendlies to Expose Young Players

items.summary: An analysis by Transparency International Australia found that bosses at ten datacentre companies secured almost 120 meetings—specifically 119—with premiers or ministers across New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, Queensland, and the ACT over a three-year period. These are the only jurisdictions to publicly release ministerial diaries, so the count reflects just those five states rather than all of Australia's decision-makers. The report argues that when combined with political donations, this access demonstrates 'unfettered' influence creating an uneven playing field for other industries.
items.title: Transparency International Australia analysis finds datacentre executives held nearly 120 meetings with state premiers and ministers over three years

items.summary:
The United Nations' COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended Sunday afternoon without consensus on its cover decision—the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity—marking the first such failure since 2009. The talks, attended by more than 100,000 participants and run two days beyond their scheduled end under Conference of the Parties president Murat Kurum of Turkey and negotiation leader Chris Bowen of Australia, still adopted several decisions, including a program to help workers transition away from fossil fuels and a plan to assess progress on climate adaptation. The deadlock stemmed primarily from deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much financing developed countries should provide to developing nations affected by climate disasters. A central aim of the meeting was to set quantifiable but voluntary global goals for economic electrification and increase funding for developing-country adaptation; these were not achieved in a unified statement.

The proposed text faced formal rejection from major blocs, including the European Union's 28-member group under Ireland's rotating presidency, several Latin American countries, and Pacific Island states. EU climate minister Darragh O'Brien stated his delegation objected because the decision omitted any mention of fossil fuels, which he called "the key driver of climate change." In contrast, Mohammad Ayoub of Saudi Arabia's energy ministry defended carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture technologies as necessary solutions to keep 1.5 degrees Celsius within reach—the long-term goal set by the 2015 Paris agreement—and noted that his country's 22-member League of Arab States supported the Antalya Pact.

The outcome reflects a broader decline in international climate collaboration since earlier agreements, including Egypt's 2022 establishment of a loss and damage fund and Dubai's 2023 adoption of language calling for a "just and orderly" fossil fuel transition by more than 190 countries. Climate envoy Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner of the Marshall Islands rejected the deal as undermining her country's security, while UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed disappointment but insisted that "this setback does not change the facts," reaffirming that fossil fuels remain driving the crisis. The article frames this outcome as a serious but non-fatal setback to global climate efforts; it notes no quantifiable targets were adopted and attributes specific objections and positions directly to named officials, while omitting any independent verification of claims about future impacts or the scientific validity of carbon capture. No chart data is provided in the source text.
items.title: UN COP31 Climate Conference Ends Without Consensus on Cover Decision

items.summary: Australian officials conceded that nations at this year's UN climate summit failed to reach an agreement, with social services minister Tanya Plibersek calling the outcome 'frustrating' and environment minister Chris Bowen describing the negotiated red lines as 'unbridgeable.' The deal fell short partly because it omitted the word 'fossil fuels,' a compromise that satisfied neither fossil fuel producers nor climate-affected nations. Deputy Liberal leader Jane Hume criticized Labor for co-hosting the summit, which ran overtime to become the longest COP ever and cost approximately $150m, while walking away without an agreement—the first since Kevin Rudd's 2009 Copenhagen failure—though Bowen defended his leadership by stating 'Australia left nothing on the field.' Concurrently, a Newspoll published in The Australian showed Labor leader Anthony Albanese trailing Coalition counterpart Angus Taylor as preferred prime minister for the first time, with Albanese's net approval rating hitting a new low of minus 31 and the Coalition's primary vote at 22% behind One Nation and Labor tied at 27%. Separately, the Lowy Institute's Asia Power Index reported that US foreign policy influence fell to its sharpest decline in nine years across eight criteria. In domestic legislative matters, communications minister Anika Wells announced a small-business carveout for digital duty of care legislation before it takes effect 12 months later, addressing business concerns about penalties exceeding $100m while the Greens continue negotiations over tougher penalties and an ombudsman.
items.title: Australia Walks Away From COP Without a Climate Deal as Albanese Trails in Newspoll

items.summary:
The Democratic Party won its largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, driven by Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseating Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's Fifth Congressional District. The race was called Sunday after a recount requested under state law because the margin fell below 1%, with Hubbard beating Foxx by **330 votes** at **99%** of ballots counted. In aggregate, Democrats hold at least **258 House seats**, matching the total Republicans held in 1992 when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats captured **258 seats**; Republicans now hold at least **173 seats**. Hubbard had lost to Foxx by nine percentage points in the 2024 midterms, but this result followed a series of Democratic upsets in deeply Republican districts across South Carolina, Texas, Alaska, and Iowa. Campaign messaging centered on rising living costs amid what candidates described as an Iran war, with President Trump and Vice President JD Vance suggesting inflation tied to that conflict contributed to the losses. Hubbard pledged to prioritize working families and small businesses while supporting public education and expanding affordable healthcare.

The party also controls the Senate alongside its House majority, giving it leverage to investigate conflicts of interest involving the president and his allies, confirm or block cabinet and judicial nominations, and advance legislation—though Trump retains veto power over enacted bills. Remaining uncalled races include Tennessee's fourth district, where Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than **300 votes**, and Minnesota's first district, where Democrat Jake Johnson is ahead by fewer than **500 votes**; two Louisiana elections will proceed to a December runoff.
items.title: Democrats Secure Largest House Majority Since 1992 After Flipping North Carolina's Fifth District

items.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, concluded without an agreement after countries failed to reach consensus on a new deal. Negotiations broke down two days past their scheduled end date, making them the longest-running talks in the summit's history. The EU and other nations rejected a fourth draft agreement because it did not include language calling for a phase-out of fossil fuels, which they identify as the largest driver of global climate change. An EU representative accused some oil-producing states of hijacking the negotiations, while Russia defended its opposition to such a commitment in remarks that included direct criticism of the EU. The report is attributed to BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard.
items.title: COP31 Climate Talks End Without a Deal After Fossil Fuel Language Dispute

items.summary: On Sunday, Nov. 22, Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number one Alexander Zverev **6**-**7**(**) on his way to winning the ATP Finals in Turin, securing his first title at the event after finishing as runner-up the previous year. The match score was reported as 6-2, 7-6(7). Alcaraz saved three set points before closing out a comeback victory that extended his streak to **14** consecutive wins and marked his third straight title of the season, having also won in Vienna and Paris. At **23**, he became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam while capturing what had been described as the biggest tour title eluding him. Since losing in the US Open quarter-finals, Alcaraz posted a **22**-**1** record across four titles. Zverev's loss ended his most successful season, during which he won his first two Grand Slam titles and rose to the top of the world rankings; as a two-time ATP Finals champion, this defeat marked an end to that run. Alcaraz had returned from a **four**-month break due to a wrist injury before the event. In the match itself, Zverev struggled with his serve and committed **19** unforced errors in the first set alone, dropping early breaks as Alcaraz took control; by the fifth game of that set he had accumulated **15** unforced errors after earning five break points against him during his first two service games. Zverev later recovered one break to narrow the deficit to **4**-**2**, but a subsequent time-violation dispute with the umpire preceded another Alcaraz break and eventual tiebreak, which he won despite failing to convert any of three consecutive set points.
items.title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev to claim maiden ATP Finals title in Turin

items.summary:
A CNBC report profiles Charles Broomfield, a 26-year-old Google employee and YouTuber who is on track to earn about $323,000 (approximately ₹3 crore) in 2026. Despite the high income, his annual living expenses remain below $20,000 (₹18.56 lakh), which CNBC notes is less than what a full-time US minimum-wage worker would earn across all 50 states at an estimated $23,700 annually. His core monthly spending in August totaled about $1,477 while he invested another $17,931 into his 401(k) and brokerage account; the breakdown included roughly $1,098 for rent and utilities (shared with four roommates), $229 for a kickboxing gym membership, $48 on Uber, about $28 on food after eating most meals at work, $15 in insurance, $59 discretionary spending, and $700 toward an employer tuition repayment plan. Sharing the apartment reportedly saves him around $1,000 monthly versus renting alone, while Google covers his Metro commute and he relies on walking, cycling, and public transit instead of owning a car.

The report attributes these habits to childhood financial training—his parents encouraged saving half of earnings—and to Broomfield's exposure at 17 to the FIRE movement via Mr. Money Mustache. After graduating from Knox College in 2022 with an early job paying more than $100,000 annually, he set a goal of accumulating $750,000 before turning 30; CNBC reports he has already built roughly $650,000 since graduation and expects to reach the target within about a year. Extreme measures are described as part of his approach, including considering living in a van parked at Google's garage and cycling two miles once to save approximately $1 on toothpaste.

The article frames this behavior primarily as a means to financial independence rather than early retirement or luxury consumption; Broomfield says he does not necessarily want to stop working and hopes instead to build an AI security business. The ultimate goal, per the report, is freedom from income anxiety—knowing he could survive losing his job tomorrow. No explicit savings percentage figure was provided in the text despite the headline's "nearly 90%" claim.

The figures are described as approximate and rounded using a stated exchange rate of US$1 = ₹93; CNBC characterizes Broomfield's $20,000 spending level as an estimate for recent years rather than a precisely verified figure. The report also notes his plans to build a business are aspirational intentions attributed to him via the outlet rather than confirmed outcomes.
items.title: Google AI security analyst Charles Broomfield saves nearly 90% of a $323,000 income while targeting financial independence before age 30

items.summary: The Indian Navy has relaxed its rules so that Naval Agniveers who choose the two-year 'Second Tour of Duty' after their initial four-year stint may marry, though only after completing mandatory professional and trade-specific training. A defence source told TOI that such personnel can then take leave for marriage purposes; the provision does not currently apply to Agniveers aged 17.5 to 21 during the initial service period under the Agnipath scheme. The relaxation arrives as the first batch, recruited in late 2022, finishes its four-year term this month and follows the Union Cabinet's approval of an extended-service option. On Nov 4, Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani announced the 'Second Tour of Duty,' extending Agniveers' service from four to six years with higher pay; continued personnel may also be enrolled as regular soldiers if they meet selection criteria and wish to stay on. Extended-tenure Agniveers are set to receive Rs 43,500 per month in the first year of extension and Rs 47,500 per month in the second year (plus allowances), with the government's Seva Nidhi contribution rising to 70% during those two years. The source noted that the Indian Army and Air Force could subsequently adopt similar marriage provisions under their own specifications.
items.title: Indian Navy permits marriage for Agniveers opting into a two-year service extension

items.summary: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra on Sunday welcomed the voter turnout in Saturday's elections, which he said reflected public demand for democracy as he appealed for participation in LAHDC (hill council) voting scheduled for Dec 4. Turnout was reported at **70.03%** in panchayat polls and **52.4%** in municipal polls; Kundra noted these were the first elections held since Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019, following the previous round in 2018. He said autonomy talks between Ladakhi representatives and the Union home ministry would resume after the LAHDC election, though he asked climate activist Sonam Wangchuk not to make provocative statements during the campaign. Kundra disputed LAB's claim that about **40%** of residents were absent from the region, stating only 10 to 12 days remained before voting and asserting that a majority had already cast ballots. He also urged Ladakhi representatives not to outright reject proposals offered by the Centre under Article 371 during MHA talks.
items.title: Ladakh chief secretary cites high panchayat turnout ahead of December 4 hill council polls
